$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.check.common.members. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-WRITEINDEX-PROJECT-FINAL
arms.note: prefer-final-public-field goes back to a project-scoped write index, so a write through a third-party subtype is invisible again

arms.name: M-WRITEINDEX-PROJECT-READONLY
arms.note: prefer-read-only-field goes back to a project-scoped write index, so a write through a third-party subtype is invisible again

arms.name: M-CHECKINDEX-PROJECT-FINAL
arms.note: prefer-final-public-field goes back to a project-scoped name/type index, so a library supertype, interface or build macro is unresolvable again

arms.name: M-CHECKINDEX-PROJECT-READONLY
arms.note: prefer-read-only-field goes back to a project-scoped name/type index, so a library supertype, interface or build macro is unresolvable again

arms.name: M-ORPHAN-UNREADABLE-ANY-FILE
arms.note: the reflection-shaped probe asks an EMPTY name, which `skippedFilesMentioning` reads as every admitted skipped file, so the per-NAME shape collapses back into the run-wide veto and an unparseable project file spelling nothing declines the deletion

arms.name: M-ORPHAN-UNREADABLE-REPORT-SCOPE
arms.note: both unreadable probes narrow back to the REPORT index, so a skip-parsing sibling in the resolution scope licenses everything again: `hxq lint <one file> --fix` with `resolutionRoots` declared DELETES a `get_x` an unparseable sibling calls, and reports a proven orphan where an unparseable subtype may declare the property

arms.name: M-ORPHAN-FIX-UNREADABLE-BLIND
arms.note: the FIX side stops asking the unreadable question at all, so an unparseable file spelling the accessor, the property or a computed accessor name blocks no deletion and no finding says why one went through

arms.name: M-ORPHAN-REPORT-UNREADABLE-BLIND
arms.note: the REPORT side stops asking it, so an unparseable file that may declare a subtype declaring the property gets the confident `Warning` back instead of the honest `Info` naming the file

arms.name: M-ORPHAN-UNREADABLE-REFLECTIVE-NARROWED
arms.note: the REFLECTION-shaped names take the per-owner narrowing too, so an unparseable installed source holding `Reflect.field(o, 'get_data')` or a computed accessor name stops vetoing a project deletion — T868's argument, unlearned one seam over

arms.name: M-ORPHAN-UNREADABLE-SUBTYPE-OWNER-WIDE
arms.note: the SUBTYPE name loses its per-owner narrowing, so one unparseable haxelib source spelling an ordinary property word declines the deletion of every accessor of that property in the project

arms.name: M-ORPHAN-REPORT-OWNER-WIDE
arms.note: the report arm loses the same narrowing, so an unparseable installed source spelling the property downgrades a proven orphan to Info and takes its deletion with it

arms.name: M-ORPHAN-ARMS-SHARE-REASON
arms.find: 'a supertype did not resolve in scope, so the property\'s absence is not proven and the method cannot be deleted'
arms.replace: 'a file in scope did not parse, so the property\'s absence is not proven and the method cannot be deleted'
arms.note: the two report-only arms decline with one sentence, so the ledger no longer says which fact stopped the edit

arms.name: M-INLINE-SUBTYPE-REPORT-INDEX
arms.note: the subtype / build-macro / interface ABSENCE questions go back to the report index, so `hxq lint <one file> --fix` inserts `inline` on a method a subtype in an unlinted file overrides — the S177 shape in the prefer-inline rule; re-encoded in S190 when the index became a per-candidate thunk

arms.name: M-INLINE-LOCAL-BUILD-MACRO
arms.note: the own-file half of the build-macro question stops being asked from the source the run already holds, so every class with a locally-eligible method builds the widest index again to answer hop zero of a closure its own file already decided — 3.21s instead of 0.12s on one file, and 18 of the 23 refusals over src + test paying for it

arms.name: M-INLINE-REFLECT-REPORT-SCOPE
arms.note: the reflection gate narrows back to the REPORT files, so `hxq lint <one file> --fix` inlines a method a `Reflect.field` in an unlinted file names — MEASURED on Haxe 4.3.7: under `--dce full` a statically-called method read reflectively answers FOUND while plain and MISSING once inline

arms.name: M-ORPHAN-ACCESSOR-REPORT-SCOPE
arms.note: the accessor-CALL scan narrows back to the REPORT files, so `hxq lint <one file> --fix` with `resolutionRoots` declared DELETES a public `get_x` a sibling file calls by hand — the S177 shape in the orphan-accessor rule, found by T895's `accessor-call` cell

arms.name: M-INLINE-UNREADABLE-BLIND
arms.note: prefer-inline's reflection gate goes blind to a scope file the parser could not read, so a method an unparseable sibling names by `Reflect.field` is folded inline and answers MISSING under --dce full — the same T867 residue as M-REFLECTION-UNREADABLE-BLIND, in the check that scans names itself

arms.name: M-FIAD-CROSS-SUPER-UNPROVED
arms.note: the crossing narrowings never hold, so every init hoisted across an explicit `super(...)` is refused again - the blanket refusal that made the rule silent on openfl display classes

arms.name: M-FIAD-EARLY-READ-IGNORED
arms.note: no occurrence of the field ever counts as observable, so an early read that compares, defaults, stores or passes on the `null` no longer refuses the crossing move

arms.name: M-FIAD-EARLY-READ-CALL-ARG
arms.replace: return parent != null && (index == 0 || parent.kind == scan.shape.callKind) && scan.faultingKinds.contains(parent.kind);
arms.note: a call ARGUMENT is admitted as a null-faulting position, so a crossing init whose field is passed on as a value moves and the callee now sees `[]` where it saw `null`

arms.name: M-FIAD-EARLY-READ-SAME-FILE
arms.note: the early-read scan looks at the field's own file only, so a subclass in another file reading the early `null` in a value position no longer refuses the move

arms.name: M-FIAD-INERT-ADMITS-ALL
arms.note: every right-hand side reads as an inert collection, so a `new`, a static call, a literal holding an identifier, a bare string or a bare scalar is hoisted ahead of the base constructor

arms.name: M-FIAD-CROSS-SUPER-NO-SOLE
arms.note: the crossing path no longer demands the sole write, so a field another member also writes moves across `super(...)` and a write the base constructor reaches outlives the deleted init

arms.name: M-FIAD-CROSS-SUPER-CHAIN
arms.note: the fix-side chain reading admits a crossing init as a co-mover, so a refused crossing init holds back the fix of an accepted one after it

arms.name: M-FIAD-DENOTES-ALL
arms.note: every occurrence of the name is read as the field, so a same-named member of an unrelated type - a bare read or a `this.` one - blocks the move

arms.name: M-FIAD-INERT-ELEMENT-ADMITS-ALL
arms.note: every collection element reads as inert, so a literal holding a foreign static read or a call is evaluated ahead of the base constructor

arms.name: M-FIAD-CROSSING-ADMITS-SCALARS
arms.find: return collectionKinds.contains(node.kind) && node.children.foreach(c -> inertElement(c, plugin, shape));
arms.replace: return collectionKinds.contains(node.kind) ? node.children.foreach(c -> inertElement(c, plugin, shape)) : ConstantFieldScan.isConstantScalarInitializer(node, plugin) || (shape.stringLiteralKinds ?? []).contains(node.kind);
arms.note: a bare scalar or string crosses `super(...)` again, although a `null` String answers `length` on hxcpp instead of faulting

arms.name: M-FIAD-TRY-IGNORED
arms.note: a faulting read inside a `try` body counts as unobservable, although the catch turns the early `null` into working code that changes once the field is initialised

arms.name: M-FIAD-NO-ROOTS-ADMITTED
arms.note: a run whose project declared no `resolutionRoots` (a `resolutionLibs`-only scope) scans the report files alone, so a narrow `--fix` moves an init a reader in an unlinted file observes

arms.name: M-FIAD-ANY-DECLARED-TYPE
arms.note: every declared type is admitted, so an abstract whose `@:from` runs code (or whose method accepts a `null` receiver) takes a hoisted literal

arms.name: M-FIAD-TRY-BOUNDARY-CLEARED
arms.find: final childInTry: Bool = inTry || (tryNode && child.kind != scan.catchKind);
arms.replace: final childInTry: Bool = !(scan.shape.functionKinds ?? []).concat(scan.shape.lambdaKinds ?? []).contains(node.kind) && (inTry || tryNode && child.kind != scan.catchKind);
arms.note: the try flag is cleared again at every function and lambda boundary, so a lambda or local function written inside a `try` and called there reads the early `null` under a catch that turns it into working code

arms.name: M-FIAD-SHADOW-IGNORED
arms.note: a core type name the file shadows - an imported, wildcard-reached or same-package user `Map` / `Array` - passes as the core type, so an abstract whose `@:from` runs code takes a hoisted literal

arms.name: M-FIAD-PROVEN-NEVER
arms.note: no crossing is ever proven, so an init after `super(...)` whose move nothing can observe is refused again whenever its right-hand side is no inert collection

arms.name: M-FIAD-PROVEN-ALWAYS
arms.note: every crossing counts as proven, with or without the truth: an init an override, a listener or a shared static can observe is hoisted ahead of the base constructor

arms.name: M-FIAD-PROVEN-NO-READER
arms.find: if (truth.mayReach(Region(file, crossed), field, Read) != Proven) return false;
arms.replace: if (false && truth.mayReach(Region(file, crossed), field, Read) != Proven) return false;
arms.note: the crossed code is never asked whether it can read the field, so a base constructor calling an override that reads it, or a listener the prefix fires, sees the value instead of nothing

arms.name: M-FIAD-PROVEN-NO-COMMUTE
arms.find: if (truth.mayReach(Region(file, crossed), { owner: r.owner, name: r.name }, changes) != Proven) return false;
arms.note: what the right-hand side reads is never checked against what the crossed code writes, so a construction reading a static the prefix sets runs before the prefix sets it

arms.name: M-FIAD-PROVEN-EXPOSED
arms.find: ?.reachBuilds() == null || MemberKinds.fieldExposed(tree, member, container, plugin, shape)
arms.note: a public field crosses too, though code outside the project may read it before the base constructor returns

arms.name: M-ISVAR-SLOTS-ANY
arms.note: every accessor slot counts as storageless, so an @:isVar over a `default` / `null` slot that has storage anyway is reported

arms.name: M-ISVAR-INIT-BLIND
arms.note: a declaration initializer is ignored, so the fix strips the metadata an `= v` needs to write the field

arms.name: M-ISVAR-SCOPE-REPORT-ONLY
arms.note: the storage scan reads the report set alone, so a one-file lint misses an override in a resolution-scope subclass that writes the field

arms.name: M-ISVAR-REFLECTION-BLIND
arms.note: a reflective string naming the property is ignored, so the fix removes a field `Reflect.field` reads by name

arms.name: M-ISVAR-RTTI-BLIND
arms.note: an @:rtti owner is judged like any other, so the fix changes the field set its runtime type information describes

arms.name: M-ISVAR-CHAIN-UNRESOLVED-ADMITTED
arms.note: an owner whose supertype chain does not resolve is judged anyway, so an ancestor the index never read may carry what reaches the field

arms.name: M-ISVAR-MACRO-FIXED
arms.note: a finding on a macro-built owner is fixed without a compiler oracle, so the metadata a builder's generated access may need is removed unverified

arms.name: M-ISVAR-MACRO-NEVER-ADMITTED
arms.note: a macro-built owner's finding is declined even under a compiler oracle, so the verified path the oracle offers never removes its metadata

arms.name: M-ISVAR-MEMBER-KEEP-BLIND
arms.find: if (retained != null && run.exists(n -> MemberKinds.META_KINDS.contains(n.kind) && n.name == retained)) return null;
arms.note: a member-level `@:keep` is ignored, so a member pinned against removal by machinery no scan models loses its storage

arms.name: M-ISVAR-EMPTY-CALL-UNFIXED
arms.note: an argument-less `@:isVar()` is reported but `fix` answers no edit and no reason for it

arms.name: M-PFF-MACRO-SILENT
arms.find: final decline: Null<String> = CtorFieldFold.macroFinalDecline(index, builders, owner, file, folded, oracleRelaxed);
arms.replace: if (index.traits.transitivelyCarriesBuildMacro(owner, file)) return; final decline: Null<String> = null;
arms.note: a macro-built owner's private field gets no finding at all, so the rule stays silent on every OpenFL Sprite subclass

arms.name: M-PFF-MACRO-FIXED
arms.note: a declined macro-built owner's field is finalized without a compiler oracle, which a builder assigning it outside the constructor breaks

arms.name: M-PFF-MACRO-NEVER-ADMITTED
arms.note: a macro-built owner's field is declined even under a compiler oracle, so the verified path never finalizes it

arms.name: M-PFPF-MACRO-SILENT
arms.find: final decline: Null<String> = CtorFieldFold.macroFinalDecline(index, index, owner, file, folded, oracleRelaxed);
arms.replace: if (index.traits.transitivelyCarriesBuildMacro(owner, file)) return; final decline: Null<String> = null;
arms.note: a macro-built owner's public field gets no finding at all, so the rule stays silent on every OpenFL Sprite subclass

arms.name: M-PFPF-MACRO-FIXED
arms.note: a declined macro-built owner's public field is finalized without a compiler oracle

arms.name: M-PFPF-MACRO-NEVER-ADMITTED
arms.note: a macro-built owner's public field is declined even under a compiler oracle

arms.name: M-OPTPARAM-COMMENT-DROPPED
arms.note: the suggested spelling drops a comment the author wrote inside the Null<...> wrapper

arms.name: M-DRA-MIDDLE-ARGUMENT
arms.note: a constant that is not the call's last argument is counted, so the fix cuts it and every later argument slides one slot left

arms.name: M-DRA-SKIPPED-SLOT
arms.note: an argument past an optional parameter is attributed to the parameter at its own index, though Haxe may have skipped a slot by type

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-SILENT
arms.note: no scratch field is ever reported or fixed

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-VALUE-TYPES-OFF
arms.note: a method called on a value type declines as if the field kept an object alive

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-NAME-UNCHECKED
arms.note: the stripped name is taken even where the method already uses it, which rebinds that use to the new local

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-DOMINANCE-OFF
arms.note: a read before any write of the call counts as dominated, so a field carrying a value between calls becomes a local

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-BRANCH-OPTIMISTIC
arms.note: a write in one arm of an `if` counts as dominating a read after it

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-CONDITIONAL-KEEPS
arms.note: a write in a loop body (or a switch arm, or a short-circuit's right side) survives the construct as if it always ran

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-TRY-ALWAYS
arms.note: a `try` body is walked as plain code, so a write it may never reach counts as dominating a read after it

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-SLOT-ANYWHERE
arms.note: the local is declared in a block whose end comes before a later use, which then names nothing

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-UNTYPED
arms.note: an untyped field is fixed with an empty annotation, which no longer keeps the field's type

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-LIFETIME-OFF
arms.note: an object with a method called on it becomes a local, though only the field kept it alive past the call

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-RECURSION-OFF
arms.find: return bodySpan == null || OccurrenceScan.referencedInRange(source, c.methodName, bodySpan.from, bodySpan.to, [], mask)
arms.note: a recursive method's scratch field becomes a local, so the outer call stops seeing what the inner one wrote

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-INIT-OFF
arms.find: if (init != null && !MemberKinds.isSideEffectFree(init, shape) && !trivialConstruction(init, file, plugin, traits))
arms.note: an initializer that calls something is dropped with the field

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-TRIVIAL-CTOR-ANY
arms.note: any constructor counts as only assigning its own fields, so a construction that traces is dropped

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-MACRO-IGNORED
arms.note: a field of a macro-built type is deleted with no oracle to typecheck the builder's view of it

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-ONE-METHOD
arms.find: refs.exists(r -> r.span == null || r.span.from < inside.from || r.span.to > inside.to)
arms.note: a field used in two methods counts as the scratch value of the last one

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-CLOSURE
arms.note: an occurrence inside a closure, which may run after the call returns, counts as the method's own

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-REFLECTION-OFF
arms.note: a field a string names, a possible `Reflect.field` target, is still reported

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-MODIFIERS
arms.note: a public field, or one carrying metadata, counts as a plain private one

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-CONFINED-OFF
arms.note: a subtype mentioning the field no longer keeps it from being reported

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-FOREIGN-OFF
arms.note: another object's member of the field's name is unrelated, so the field of another instance is missed

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-WRITE-ONLY
arms.note: a field the method only writes is reported as a scratch value

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-RTTI-OFF
arms.note: a field of an `@:rtti` type, reachable by name at run time, is reported

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-CTOR-RECURSES
arms.note: a constructor's own `new` of another object reads as a recursive call, so every scratch field of a constructor that constructs is declined

arms.name: M-MO-INLINE-BOUNDARY-OFF
arms.note: `separateInlineSubgroup` reads no boundary at all, so the option is accepted and does nothing: the blank it asks for is still reported as a gap inside one rank group, and a glued boundary is never flagged

arms.name: M-MO-INLINE-OPTION-IGNORED
arms.note: the inline-subgroup blank is demanded whatever the config says, so every project (the option's default is OFF) gets its tight constant groups split

arms.name: M-MO-INLINE-CONDITIONAL-BOUNDARY
arms.note: a boundary is read inside an `#if` block too, where inline and non-inline members carry no sub-order and interleave freely

arms.name: M-MO-INLINE-SEPARATOR-DROPPED
arms.note: the reorder rebuild stops reading `wantedBlanks` and joins every same-rank field pair with a bare newline, so a reordered type comes out without the inline-subgroup blank or the writer's doc-comment / multi-line blank the check then demands

arms.name: M-MO-INLINE-REPORT-UNREAD
arms.note: the REPORT path ignores the option, so it flags the very blank the option asks for while the fix path inserts it

arms.name: M-MO-INLINE-FIX-UNREAD
arms.note: the FIX path ignores the option, so a boundary finding re-derives as no issue there and is never fixed

arms.name: M-MO-INLINE-MESSAGE-AS-RANK
arms.find: case InlineBoundary: 'the inline members of a rank group are not separated from the rest of it by a blank line';
arms.replace: case InlineBoundary: 'rank groups are not separated by a blank line';
arms.note: a missing blank at the inline-subgroup boundary is reported as a missing RANK-group blank, naming a boundary that is not there

arms.name: M-MO-INLINE-BOUNDARY-BEFORE-EXEMPTIONS
arms.note: the boundary is asked before the non-field and comment-led exemptions, so a same-rank method pair and a line-comment-led field are demanded a blank they never were

arms.name: M-MO-INLINE-BOUNDARY-AT-LEAST-ONE
arms.replace: want.atLeast || want.rule == InlineBoundary ? blanks < want.count : blanks != want.count
arms.note: the boundary wants AT LEAST one blank instead of exactly one, so two blank lines there are left standing

arms.name: M-MO-INLINE-CONDITIONAL-REBUILD-UNREAD
arms.replace: MemberSpacing.separatorBetween(prevMember, m, source, { separateInline: false, writer: spacing.writer })
arms.note: the `#if`-region rebuild ignores the option, so a type with any conditional member loses the inline-subgroup blank on reorder

arms.name: M-MO-INLINE-SPACING-ONLY-UNREAD
arms.find:
reported.declineReason = pinned;
		MemberSpacing.emitSpacingOnly(edits, members, source, spacing);
arms.replace:
reported.declineReason = pinned;
		MemberSpacing.emitSpacingOnly(edits, members, source, { separateInline: false, writer: spacing.writer });
arms.note: the spacing-only fallback of a pinned container ignores the option, so its glued boundary is reported for ever and never fixed

arms.name: M-MO-WRITER-REPORT-UNREAD
arms.note: the REPORT path ignores the writer's member-gap policy, so it flags a blank the writer forces (the 44 client blanks around multi-line fields) while the fix path - reading the policy - finds nothing to do

arms.name: M-MO-WRITER-FIX-UNREAD
arms.note: the FIX path ignores the writer's member-gap policy, so a doc-commented field the report flags re-derives as no issue there and is never set off

arms.name: M-MO-WRITER-DOC-IGNORED
arms.note: the writer's doc-comment rule is not asked, so a glued doc-commented field stays exempt and `lint` is silent about the blanks `fmt` then adds

arms.name: M-MO-WRITER-MULTILINE-IGNORED
arms.note: the writer's multi-line rule is not asked, so the blank `aroundMultilineFields` writes around a multi-line field is reported as a gap inside one rank group, for ever - the fix's edit is undone by the canonical round-trip

arms.name: M-MO-WRITER-UNMEASURABLE-GUESS
arms.note: a slot the multi-line measure cannot read is guessed to be one-line, so the check demands a tight gap the writer may keep open

arms.name: M-MO-WRITER-CONDITIONAL
arms.find: a.condition == null && b.condition == null ? spacing.writer : null
arms.note: the writer's member-gap policy is applied inside an `#if` body too, whose members the writer writes with their source gaps

arms.name: M-MO-WRITER-CONTAINER-KIND
arms.note: the writer's member-gap policy is applied to a container kind the writer does not run it on

arms.name: M-MO-WRITER-MINIMUM-AS-EXACT
arms.note: the writer's doc / multi-line blank is read as an EXACT count, though the writer keeps a fuller gap as the source has it, so two blanks before a doc-commented method are reported against a writer that writes them

arms.name: M-DEFAULT-ARG-NULL-SITE-ADMITTED
arms.note: a call passing null where the default lands is ignored, so it silently takes the default

arms.name: M-DEFAULT-ARG-NONNULL-ANY
arms.note: every argument counts as non-null, a variable or a call included

arms.name: M-DEFAULT-ARG-UNRESOLVED-NULL-IGNORED
arms.replace: if (called != null && resolveCallee(call, owner, entry, scope, seams) != null)
arms.note: only resolved calls are read, so a null handed through a receiver the rule cannot type escapes

arms.name: M-DEFAULT-ARG-NULL-CONST-NONNULL
arms.note: an inline constant whose value is null proves its argument non-null

arms.name: M-OVERRIDDEN-INLINE-FIX-NONE
arms.note: the fix finds the overridden method's inline modifier and deletes nothing, so --fix leaves the override failing in every build that compiles it

arms.name: M-RTTI-HOMONYM-REFUSES
arms.note: the @:rtti gate reads every declaration of the owner's simple name again, so another package's @:rtti namesake refuses the enum-abstract conversion

arms.name: M-PLAN-GUARDED-META-ALLOWED
arms.note: a conditional region of metadata above the type no longer refuses the enum-abstract conversion, so `#if !x @:keep #end class C` converts and the build that keeps the region loses the kept class

arms.name: M-TRIVIAL-GETTER-GRANTEE-UNSEEN
arms.note: trivial-getter asks the subtype graph alone again, so a backing field a grantee reads is deleted by a collapse that rewrites only the owner

arms.name: M-TRIVIAL-GETTER-ACCESSOR-UNSEEN
arms.note: trivial-getter deletes an accessor a subtype or a grantee calls by name, guarding the backing field alone

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-UNSTORED-BLIND
arms.note: the setter of a property it never stores is fixed like any method, so the field holding the value it forgot to store becomes a local and the evidence is gone

arms.name: M-SCRATCH-MEMBER-NAME-TAKEN
arms.note: the stripped name is taken even when a member of the type holds it, so the local shadows that member in the method

arms.name: M-UNSTORED-INIT-BLIND
arms.note: a declaration initializer is not seen as a store, so a property whose field holds that value is reported as never stored

arms.name: M-UNSTORED-REFLECTION-BLIND
arms.note: a reflective string naming the property is ignored, although Reflect.setField writes its field by name

arms.name: M-UNSTORED-META-ADMITTED
arms.note: metadata on the property is ignored, so the fix rewrites the read access of a property a macro or the runtime may reach

arms.name: M-UNSTORED-KEEP-ADMITTED
arms.note: a @:keep owner is fixed like any other, although its field may be reached by name

arms.name: M-UNSTORED-RTTI-ADMITTED
arms.note: an @:rtti owner is fixed like any other, so the access its runtime type information describes changes

arms.name: M-UNSTORED-CHAIN-ADMITTED
arms.note: an owner whose supertype chain does not resolve is fixed anyway, although an unseen supertype may declare the property with the access it must keep

arms.name: M-UNSTORED-EXTERN-ADMITTED
arms.note: an extern owner is judged like a class, although the native side stores its field where no text shows it

arms.name: M-UNSTORED-DYNAMIC-WRITE-BLIND
arms.note: a write through Dynamic is not seen as a store, so the fix removes a field that write needs and the program fails at run time

arms.name: M-UNSTORED-ENUMERATION-ADMITTED
arms.note: code listing or rendering an object's fields is ignored, so the fix changes what it prints

arms.name: M-STATICINIT-ANY-ORDER
arms.note: a read of a static declared above the reader is flagged too

arms.name: M-STATICINIT-NO-DEFERRED
arms.note: a read inside a function literal counts as an eager read

arms.name: M-STATICINIT-BY-NAME
arms.find: declaredAt(members, name, Refs.bindingAt(name, span.from, tree, shape))
arms.note: an identifier is matched to a field by its spelling, not by the declaration it binds

arms.name: M-STATICINIT-ANY-QUALIFIER
arms.note: another type's static of the same name counts as a read of the field

arms.name: M-STATICINIT-CALLS-NOT-ENTERED
arms.note: a static method the initializer calls is never entered, so a later field its body reads is missed

arms.name: M-STATICINIT-REFERENCE-RUNS
arms.note: a method named as a value reads as run, so its body's reads are flagged though nothing calls it at initialization

arms.name: M-DRA-NONLITERAL-INLINE
arms.note: any inline constant other than null reads as a default, so the fix writes a concatenated string constant as a default Haxe refuses as not constant

arms.name: M-PAM-GRANT-PUBLIC
arms.note: a public member read under the waiver gets its type granted too

arms.name: M-MEMBER-ORDER-IDENTITY-UNWIRED
arms.note: member-order names no identity of its own again, so the neighbour in its message keys the finding
